source.paper: B. Benson, P. Ralli, P. Tetali, "Volume growth, curvature, and Buser-type inequalities in graphs"
source.label: Conjecture 4.1, Section 4.2 (with Definition 2.1, Example 1)

exact_statement_and_quantifiers: Definition 2.1: mu_x = 1/2 at x, 1/(2 d_x) on each neighbour; kappa(x,y)=1-W1(mu_x,mu_y)/d(x,y). Conjecture 4.1: Let G be a pq-regular graph such that for all u,v in V(G), kappa(u,v) >= (2-p)/(pq). Let x in V(G), y in V(T_p^q). Then for any i>=0, |dist_x^{-1}(i)| <= |dist_y^{-1}(i)|. (T_p infinite p-regular tree; T_p^q Cartesian power.) Source explicitly highlights the case p=2: Z^d has fastest volume growth among 2d-regular graphs with curvature >= 0.
claim: Conjecture 4.1 is false for (p,q)=(2,2) (finite counterexample) and for (p,q)=(2,q), q>=3 (infinite counterexamples H x Z^{q-2}).
construction: G = AGL(1,5) as permutation group on {0..4}; S = {a, a^-1, c, d} with a=(0 3 1 2), c=(0 3)(2 4), d=(0 2)(1 4) (right Cayley graph, permutations composed as (u*v)(i)=u(v(i))). H = Cay(G,S): 20 vertices, 4-regular, triangle-free, non-bipartite.

decisive_calculation_executed.results: Exact W1 via 8-unit assignment (masses multiples of 1/8): kappa in {0,1/8} on all 40 edges; min over all 190 pairs = 0. Spheres from every vertex [1,4,9,6] vs T_2^2=Z^2 [1,4,8,12]: |S_2|=9>8. H x Z (6-regular, infinite, vertex-transitive): explicit-plan lower bound kappa>=0 on all generator edges; spheres to radius 2 [1,6,19] vs Z^3 [1,6,18].
decisive_calculation_executed.consistency: Source Theorem 4.4 (d=4,k=0) proves |S_2|<=10; 9 lies in the gap between proven 10 and conjectured 8. H non-bipartite, so Theorem 4.5 (bound 8) does not apply.

proof_route: (1) Explicit coupling bound: for an edge xy of a d-regular graph with A=N(x)\N[y], B=N(y)\N[x], |A|=|B|, keep common mass, move (d-1)/(2d) from x to y, transport A->B by a bijection sigma: W1 <= ((d-1)+sum d(a,sigma a))/(2d). (2) For H: exact enumeration (or the same plan) gives kappa>=0 on edges; Ollivier edge-to-pairs (source Theorem 2.1) or direct all-pairs enumeration gives all pairs. (3) BFS spheres. (4) Products: for H x Z^k the plan with parallel matching of the extra-coordinate neighbours gives M <= d+1 on every edge orbit, hence kappa>=0; |S_2(H x Z^k)| = 9+8k+2k^2 > 2(k+2)^2 = |S_2(Z^{k+2})| for all k>=0 (the general-k product lemma is proved on paper only; k=1 checked).
certificate_size: Graph of 20 vertices / 40 edges; 40 edge couplings with rational masses in 1/8; BFS. Lean: finite decidable computation over Fin 20 plus rational transport inequalities; W1 lower-bound side not needed (only upper bound on W1 via explicit plan). Main formal burden: defining Wasserstein/Ollivier curvature and T_2^2 sphere sizes (|S_2(Z^2)|=8 finite check).
strongest_objections: PRIOR/PUBLIC OBJECT (likely fatal): Bai-Lu-Yau, "Ricci-flat graphs with maximum degree at most 4", arXiv:2103.00941v2 (2021), Theorem 11/Figure 35 publish a 20-vertex 4-regular Ricci-flat (LLY) graph in Section 4.2 (C3-free class) with no two C4 sharing an edge. Then each edge lies in exactly one C4, each vertex in exactly two C4s, so |S_2|=12-2=10>8 at every vertex; LLY-Ricci-flat implies lazy-1/2 kappa=0 (idleness linearity, Bourne et al., cited as [16] in BRT). This is a hand deduction from the text; Figure 35 adjacency was NOT machine-extracted. Figure 29 shows two further finite 4-regular Ricci-flat graphs (adjacency not extracted). Hence a counterexample to Conj 4.1 is plausibly a routine corollary of a public classification, though no source found stating it.

No source found (bounded arXiv search, 5 BRT-related queries plus 7 fetched closest bodies) that cites or refutes BRT Conjecture 4.1; successors 2512.03968v2, 2607.27162v1, 2608.14232v1 treat the Bishop-Gromov analogue as largely open and do not cite BRT. Absence of hits is NOT clearance.

Scope: conjecture is about volume growth; a finite graph or a local radius-2 failure may be judged against the spirit (BRT motivation is polynomial growth, now proved for transitive graphs by 2512.03968). The literal statement quantifies over all pq-regular graphs and all i>=0, so the finite example is in scope; H x Z gives an infinite one for q=3.
Routine-adaptation risk: easy kappa>=0 families (abelian, conjugation-invariant S) exist (2608.14232 Example 1.7); our S is not conjugation-invariant, but small Cayley searches are routine.

source.paper: M. C. Dourado, S. Ehard, L. D. Penso, D. Rautenbach, "Partial immunization of trees"
source.label: Conjecture 1.3 with definitions (2), Theorem 1.2

exact_statement_and_quantifiers: For a given graph G and integer b with 0<=b<=2m(G), there is a matching M of G such that vacc(G,0,d_G,b) <= 2 dyn(G,tau_M) and tau_M(V(G)) <= b, where tau_M(u)=d_G(u) if u is incident with [an edge of] M and 0 otherwise; vacc(G,tau,iota_max,b)=max{dyn(G,tau+iota): iota integer, 0<=iota<=iota_max, iota(V)=b}; dyn = minimum order of a dynamic monopoly (hull adds u with |H cap N(u)|>=tau(u)).
claim: False for G=K3, b=3 (and K4, b in {4,5}; 12 graphs on <=5 vertices).

decisive_calculation_executed.hand: K3,b=3: iota=(1,1,1) has dyn=1 (empty set closed), so vacc>=1 (in fact =1). Any nonempty matching has tau_M(V)=4>3, so only M=empty is admissible, dyn(K3,0)=0, and 1<=0 fails.
decisive_calculation_executed.results: Exhaustive n<=5 (52 isomorphism classes): 12 failing graphs, every failure at a budget b below min over nonempty matchings of tau_M(V) ("boundary"), always vacc=1. 150 random labelled n=6 graphs (seed 7): 18 boundary-only failures, 0 non-boundary.

proof_route: Complete as stated (finite check). General mechanism: any graph with a cycle C_k and b with k<=b<min_{uv}(d(u)+d(v)) where thresholds 1 on a cycle are affordable.
certificate_size: 3 vertices; trivially formalizable once dyn/vacc are defined.
strongest_objections: Endpoint/domain correction: failure only where no nonempty matching fits the budget; obvious repair (b >= min edge cost, or a relaxed matching condition) restores plausibility; credit standard excludes such corrections.
